advances: Exact seven-base reduction for independently varying contained additions in dimension d≥2 and fixed core simplex. The expansion is conditional on the six-base local coefficient.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The base hull is the quadrilateral given by $-1\le z_1\le1$, $z_2\le1$, $z_1+2z_2\ge-1$, since its vertices are $r,p,p',(1,1)$. At integer first coordinates $-1,0,1$, its integer second coordinates are respectively $\{0,1\},\{0,1\},\{-1,0,1\}$. The three added bases uniquely maximize $-2z_1-z_2,-z_1+z_2,z_1-2z_2$, respectively. Hence their fibers are the placed bodies. Each continuous generator lies in $T$ and each core base has a full copy of $T$, so its fiber stays $T$. Summing the volumes gives $M_t$.

Write $F_T(y,u)=|T\cap\{u\cdot x\ge u\cdot y\}|$ for unit $u$. For fixed $t$, e6ed7f0a4aa574cd applies with the actual coefficients $a_t,c_t>0$. It gives the exact six-base depth at $(q,y)$ as the minimum of $F_T(y,u)$ plus the two opposite-shift cap masses, with shifts $|s|\le D+1$ for $D=\operatorname{diam}T$. Its realizing tilt is $\beta=(-K+s/2,-K-s/2)$ for $K=D+(D+1)/2+1$, in the cap of margin $u\cdot(x-y)+\beta\cdot z$. The margin on $r$ is at least $-D+K-s/2\ge1$. Thus the realizing cap also fully captures $R_t$ in the seven-base hull. For every $y\in T$ this bounds seven-base depth above by $tw_t$ plus six-base depth. By testing a canonical direction with $\lambda_i(y)\ge b$ and saturating the smaller pair mass, the upper bound is at most $\Gamma V+t(w_t+\min(a_t,c_t))$.

Every containing cap can be tightened through $(q,y)$. If it has nonzero continuous normal and does not contain the whole $R_t$, its threshold at $r$ is strictly above $m_u=\min_T u\cdot x$. At the opposite core $(1,0)$ the threshold is below $2u\cdot y-m_u$. The own and opposite core costs alone are at least
$$
F_T(y,u)+|T\cap\{u\cdot x\ge2u\cdot y-m_u\}|.
$$
At $g$ this is at least $(\Gamma+\rho_d)V$ with $\rho_d>0$ from 53fe12b742a7608d. The expression is jointly continuous in $y,u$ by hyperplane nullity, including at support levels, and the unit sphere is compact. On a fixed neighborhood $U$ it is at least $(\Gamma+\rho_d/2)V$. A pure-base cap through $q$ contains its entire simplex, and $V>(\Gamma+\rho_d/2)V$ since $\rho_d<\Gamma<1/2$ for $d\ge2$. For sufficiently small $t$ these lower bounds exceed the constructed upper bound. Every remaining cap contains all of $R_t$ and pays at least the six-base depth on the six retained fibers. This proves the local identity on $U$.

For fixed $t$ depth is upper semicontinuous on each fiber: a containing cap with mass below a given number can be enlarged by a sufficiently small outward parallel translation to cover a neighborhood of its mark and keep the mass below that number, by continuity from above. Compactness gives attainment. Each $q$-fiber maximum is at least $\Gamma V$ from its own centroid. For every canonical direction $i$, the same tilt and saturation give depth at most $V(1-\lambda_i(y))^d+t(w_t+\min(a_t,c_t))$ in either hull. At a maximizer this implies $\lambda_i(y)\le b+O(t)$ uniformly for each $i$. Since the coordinates sum to one, each is $b+O(t)$, giving $y=g+O(t)$. Therefore both sets lie in $U$ and the local identity makes the sets coincide and adds $tw_t$ to the local maximum.

For $(0,1)$ use the retained collinear fibers $A_t,T,T$ at $p,(0,1),(1,1)$. For $(1,0)$ use $C_t,T,T$ at $p',(1,0),(1,1)$. In each case their bases identify affinely with $-1,0,1$. Restrict a containing cap to their affine span. The result is either a containing cap or the whole triple, both of mass at least the lower bound at the middle centroid in 98603e266680b22d, since $ta_t,tc_t\le\rho_dV$ for small $t$. For the matching caps put $\delta(z)=z_1+2(1-z_2)$ at the first anchor and $\delta(z)=1-z_1+z_2$ at the second. Each vanishes at its anchor, equals $-1$ at its selected addition and is at least one on every other site in the census. The caps $\lambda_i(x)-2\delta(z)\ge b$ have exactly the claimed masses and cover the anchor simplex. If $y\ne g$, use a coordinate $\lambda_i(y)>b$ and raise that cap's threshold to $\lambda_i(y)$, strictly reducing the own mass. For $(1,1)$ the same canonical cover with $\delta(z)=2-z_1-z_2$ isolates its own trace, while its centroid gives the lower bound. The exposing pure-base caps at the additions bound their depths by their masses, all below $\Gamma V$ for small $t$.

The census and exact local maxima now give the global formula. The finite maximum of the three first-order expansions gives $L$, and division by $M_t$ gives the normalized formula. A strictly largest coefficient produces a strict gap for sufficiently small $t$, and the side-anchor uniqueness was proved above.

source_sections.locator: 501dba519aa398a9:01 Setup and §1 (2)–(5), actual seven fibers and local identity

statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $T\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full simplex of volume $V$ and centroid $g$. Let $\lambda_i$ be its barycentric coordinates and $\ell_i$ their linear parts for $0\le i\le d$. Set $b=1/(d+1)$, $\Gamma=(1-b)^d$ and $\kappa=dV(1-b)^{d-1}$. At each of the four bases in $\{0,1\}^2$ place $T$. At $r=(-1,0)$, $p=(-1,1)$ and $p'=(1,-1)$ place convex bodies $R_t,A_t,C_t\subseteq T$ of respective volumes $t w_t,t a_t,t c_t$, where $(w_t,a_t,c_t)\to(w,a,c)\in(0,\infty)^3$ as $t\downarrow0$. Take their lifted convex hull and use the sum of $d$-volumes on the actual integer fibers and all closed ambient halfspaces. The auxiliary six-base hull deletes the generator at $r$. Let $q=(0,0)$, let $D_{6,t}^0$ and $D_{7,t}^0$ be the maximum raw depths on the $q$ fibers, and let $D_{7,t}$ be the global maximum raw depth in the seven-base hull.

The seven listed sites are precisely the actual integer fibers, with their placed bodies unchanged, and the total mixed volume is $M_t=4V+t(w_t+a_t+c_t)$. There is a fixed neighborhood $U\subseteq T$ of $g$ such that for every sufficiently small $t$ and every $y\in U$ the raw depth at $(q,y)$ in the seven-base hull is its six-base raw depth plus $tw_t$. All local maxima are attained. The full sets of $q$-fiber maximizers coincide for sufficiently small $t$ and all their marks are $O(t)$ from $g$, so $D_{7,t}^0=tw_t+D_{6,t}^0$.

At bases $(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)$ the raw local maxima are respectively $\Gamma V+ta_t$, $\Gamma V+tc_t$ and $\Gamma V$ for sufficiently small $t$. The first two occur only at $g$ in their fibers. Every added-fiber mark has depth at most the mass of its fiber. Thus
$$
D_{7,t}=\Gamma V+\max\{ta_t,tc_t,tw_t+D_{6,t}^0-\Gamma V\}.
$$
In particular, if $D_{6,t}^0=\Gamma V+t\bar J+o(t)$ and $L=\max\{a,c,w+\bar J\}$, then
$$
D_{7,t}=\Gamma V+tL+o(t),\qquad
\frac{D_{7,t}}{M_t}=\frac{\Gamma}{4}
+t\frac{4L-\Gamma(w+a+c)}{16V}+o(t).
$$
A strictly largest term among $a,c,w+\bar J$ forces every global maximizer into its corresponding base $(0,1),(1,0),q$. In the first two cases the centroid there is the unique global maximizer.
title: Exact local and global depth reduction in a seven-base simplex hull
